title: IonQ Stock News (Oct 16, 2026): IONQ Rises 9.3% to $34.35
summary: IonQ (IONQ) closed up 9.33% at $34.35 on Oct 15, 2026, rebounding a day after its $2.0 billion equity offering sent shares lower.
body_markdown:
## Why IonQ Stock Rose


We found no new company announcement dated October 15, so the move reads as a recovery from the prior day's selloff. As reported by[StockStory](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/stocks-making-big-moves-yesterday-172827052.html) , IonQ fell 5.2% on Wednesday, October 14, after the company announced the pricing of a $2.0 billion equity offering, which it said would accelerate the commercialization of its full-stack quantum platform.


According to[24/7 Wall St.](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/quantum-computing-stocks-rebound-dilution-154659409.html) , the deal was sold to a single institutional buyer in a mix of common shares and pre-funded warrants, priced below IonQ's recent trading level. The outlet reported that pure-play quantum names bounced on October 15, with IonQ and Rigetti up about 3% and D-Wave up about 2% at the time of writing, while the Defiance Quantum ETF slipped. IonQ extended that early gain to 9.33% by the close.


## IONQ Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- Per 24/7 Wall St., second-quarter 2026 revenue reached $80.05 million, up 286.8% year over year, and IonQ raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $280 million to $290 million.
- The company said the $2.0 billion raise will fund commercialization of its full-stack quantum platform, according to StockStory.
- Per[Motley Fool](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/ionq-following-nvidias-playbook-why-224300097.html) , IonQ has built out its stack through acquisitions, including the SkyWater foundry earlier this year and the recently announced Elisity security deal.


### Risks


- The offering adds to a share count of 405.1 million at the latest quarter, and 24/7 Wall St. noted the warrant structure means dilution could arrive in stages.
- The stock remains 53.50% below its 52-week high, and Motley Fool described it as down around 60% from its highs.
- 24/7 Wall St. reported a diluted loss of $3.43 per share over the past 12 months, so the company is not yet profitable.
